title: Get started with bruce
text: bruce_simulate() invents 30 km city two hills, urban core, 12 reference stations, 40 low-cost sensors read 1.5 °C warm, coarse reanalysis-like background. returns “true” temperature every pixel, real data never gives us.
code: library(bruce) sim <- bruce_simulate(n_reference = 12, n_biased = 40, n_days = 5, seed = 1)  head(sim$obs) #>   station_id       date    value    truth #> 1      REF01 2025-01-01 27.61612 27.36747 #> 2      REF02 2025-01-01 27.74348 27.75385 #> 3      REF03 2025-01-01 28.51989 28.04309 #> 4      REF04 2025-01-01 27.01882 27.10761 #> 5      REF05 2025-01-01 29.10219 28.70484 #> 6      REF06 2025-01-01 27.62704 27.98792 sim$sources #>      source  bias obs_sd #> 1 reference FALSE    0.3 #> 2   lowcost  TRUE     NA op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(2, 2, 3, 4)) terra::plot(sim$covariates$elev, main = "Elevation (m)",             col = hcl.colors(50, "Terrain 2")) terra::plot(sim$covariates$urb, main = "Urban fraction",             col = hcl.colors(50, "Grays", rev = TRUE)) terra::plot(sim$truth[[3]], main = "True temperature, day 3",             col = hcl.colors(50, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE)) ref <- sim$stations$source == "reference" points(sim$stations$x, sim$stations$y, pch = ifelse(ref, 24, 21),        bg = "white", cex = 0.7) par(op)

text: day--day correlation field drifts 1 (failure seen clustered sensor networks), bruce_fit() restarts optimiser , needed, refits correlation fixed. Every attempt recorded.

title: Get started with bruce
text: bruce_decompose() splits day’s surface part explained covariates spatial field learned stations, reports much spatial variance carries, including covariance.
code: pred <- bruce_predict(fit, n_samples = 200, keep_samples = TRUE) terra::plot(pred$mean[[3]])  dec <- bruce_decompose(fit) plot(dec, date = "2025-01-03")   # total, covariate part, spatial field  zones <- sf::st_sf(zone = "city", geometry = sf::st_geometry(sim$domain)) bruce_zonal(pred, zones, "zone")  # long table (cell x day) for dplyr/ggplot2 library(dplyr); library(ggplot2) as_tibble(pred) |>   filter(date == min(date)) |>   ggplot(aes(x, y, fill = mean)) + geom_raster() + coord_equal()

title: bruce: Bayesian urban climate estimation
text: Bayesian Rio Urban Climate Estimator, generalised city. bruce interpolates daily urban air temperature fusing observation networks different quality — official stations, airports, low-cost IoT sensors, citizen weather stations — optional gridded background (e.g. ERA5-Land). developed Rio de Janeiro’s heat surveillance written city comparable data can use : everything city-specific enters small data contract.

title: bruce: Bayesian urban climate estimation
text: observation network k station , location s, day t: η = β₀ + δₖ + x(s)ᵀβ + uᵢ + dₜ + w(s, t) δₖ — offset biased network (estimated networks declared bias = TRUE) x(s)ᵀβ — spatial covariates (elevation, urban fraction, …) uᵢ — iid station effect (persistent siting bias) dₜ — city-wide daily AR(1) term w(s, t) — Matérn SPDE field AR(1) dependence days network (background) Gaussian likelihood fixed PC-prior observation standard deviation. Windows (one month tested scale) fitted independently R-INLA.

title: bruce: Bayesian urban climate estimation
code: install.packages("INLA", repos = c(getOption("repos"),                  INLA = "https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/stable"), dep = TRUE) remotes::install_github("asgouveiaa/bruce")

title: bruce: Bayesian urban climate estimation

title: bruce: Bayesian urban climate estimation
code: library(bruce) sim  <- bruce_simulate(seed = 1)          # or your own city's data  d    <- bruce_data(sim$obs, sim$stations, sim$sources, crs = sim$crs,                    background = sim$background) d    <- bruce_covariates(d, sim$covariates) mesh <- bruce_mesh(d) fit  <- bruce_fit(d, mesh, bruce_spec(), keep_config = TRUE) bruce_check(fit)                          # every attempt, collapse diagnostics  pred <- bruce_predict(fit, n_samples = 200, keep_samples = TRUE) expo <- bruce_zonal(pred, zones, id_col = "zone", weights = population) cv   <- bruce_cv(d, mesh, scheme = "lso", checkpoint_dir = "cv_lso")

title: bruce: Bayesian urban climate estimation
text: clustered networks day--day correlation field can drift 1 variance explode. bruce_fit() checks every fit , default, restarts mode search reset point , also collapses, refits correlation fixed (fallback_group_rho, default 0.55). attempts kept fit$attempts; fit$status records outcome. See ?bruce_spec (on_collapse).

title: Model specification — bruce_spec
text: range_prior PC prior Matern range: "nn" anchors median median nearest-neighbour distance stations (resolution limit network), give number metres. Rio de Janeiro application uses 15000; "nn" default adapts network without city-specific constant. range_prior_prob Probability range range_prior. sigma_prior PC prior field standard deviation, c(u, p) meaning P(sigma > u) = p. group_rho_prior PC prior (pc.cor1) day--day AR(1) correlation spatial field. group_rho_fixed Fix correlation value instead estimating . station_effect Include iid station random effect (absorbs persistent station-level siting bias). station_prior PC prior standard deviation. day_effect Include city-wide daily AR(1) term. day_rho_prior, day_prec_prior Priors daily term. day_sd_fixed Fix daily term's standard deviation instead estimating . biased_prec_prior PC prior observation standard deviation networks obs_sd = NA. intercept_prior c(mean, precision) intercept; NA mean uses mean reference observations. covariate_prec, bias_prec Prior precision covariate network offset coefficients (mean 0). int_strategy INLA integration strategy. on_collapse fit degenerates (field day--day correlation near 1, field standard deviation exploding): "retry_then_fix" restarts reset mode , collapses , refits correlation fixed fallback_group_rho; "fix" goes straight fixed refit; "warn" warns; "none" nothing. collapse_rho, collapse_sd_ratio Thresholds collapse check: fit flagged posterior mean correlation exceeds collapse_rho field standard deviation exceeds collapse_sd_ratio times standard deviation observations. fallback_group_rho Value used correlation must fixed. num_threads Passed INLA (NULL uses INLA's default).

title: bruce 0.1.0 (em desenvolvimento, repositório privado)
text: Primeira versão. Funções: Contrato de dados: bruce_data() (observações, estações, redes de referência e enviesadas, background opcional) e bruce_covariates() (cada covariável lida próprio raster, na sua projeção e resolução; na_value para áreas sem dado). Modelo: bruce_mesh() (contorno com o mesmo algoritmo INLA), bruce_spec() (priors, termos, tratamento de colapso), bruce_fit() (detecção colapso campo e aviso quando malha é grossa demais para o range estimado) e bruce_check(). Uso ajuste: bruce_predict(), bruce_decompose() com plot(), bruce_zonal(). Saídas em tabela são tibbles (bruce_cv(), bruce_zonal(), bruce_decompose()$variance); as_tibble() converte predição e decomposição em tabela longa (célula × dia) para dplyr/ggplot2. Validação: bruce_cv() (LSO e LRO, CRPS, cobertura, checkpoints) e bruce_simulate() (cidade sintética). Registro da validação com o Rio de Janeiro (mediana, janeiro de 2025) em analises/rio/README.md.
